Disorder of cutaneous sweat glands causing colored sweat.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy from a GPI-anchor biosynthesis disorder; joint hypermobility occurs in 20/20, supporting musculoskeletal involvement.
Renal tubular degeneration defines nephronophthisis; retinal degeneration in 1/3 meets the approximate threshold, with limited evidence. Anemia is secondary to renal failure.

Cerebellar malformation and intellectual disability define disease; polydactyly 6/9, retinal dystrophy 3/8, hearing loss 1/1. Hearing evidence is sparse; infections alone do not prove immunodeficiency.
Intellectual disability, scalp aplasia and urethral hypospadias are defining features, each 80-99%; digital syndactyly occurs in 30-79% and clinodactyly in 80-99%.
Motor neuronopathy with spasticity defines disease; distal muscle atrophy occurs in 85-100%, fatty muscle replacement in 2/4 and fixed foot deformities in about 46-69%.
Sterile serous effusion affects the middle ear; infection or an immune mechanism is not required across the concept.
Acute myocardial inflammation and necrosis, generally infectious or immune-mediated, define the disease.
Eyelid/lacrimal defects, dystonia and digital malformations define syndrome; hearing impairment occurs in 30-79%. Cleft palate, also 30-79%, omitted because of the cap.
Isolated congenital defect of the oral palate; nonspecific neurological annotations do not define this nonsyndromic concept.
Nonsyndromic hereditary hearing loss affects the auditory system.
Hydrocephalus, intellectual disability and spastic diplegia define syndrome; scoliosis occurs frequently (30-79%). Hearing and optic abnormalities are occasional.
Defective renal tubules define disease; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 80-99%. Skull ossification defects and arthrogryposis are major features; joint hypermobility occurs in 80-99%.
Hair and tooth abnormalities define this ectodermal dysplasia; brittle hair and oligodontia each occur in 56/56.
Motor pathway degeneration and neuropathy define disease; lasting distal muscle atrophy is frequent (30-79%). Abnormal saccades reflect neurological dysfunction.
Developmental disability and limb abnormalities define syndrome; limited elbow extension in 4/5. Ptosis affects eyelid function in 2/5; hirsutism alone does not establish skin damage.
Skeletal dysplasia with joint abnormalities defines disease; intellectual disability occurs in 3/4. Neonatal respiratory distress in 3/9 does not establish lasting pulmonary damage.
HbS/HbO-Arab hemoglobinopathy causes red-cell sickling and hemolysis; specific organ complications vary and are often separately diagnosed.
Phenytoin poisoning primarily causes CNS and cerebellar dysfunction. The poisoning parent supports this interpretation; the related fetal hydantoin synonym does not define additional organs.
Inherited cardiac calcium-release dysfunction causes ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death.
Compression neuropathy of the posterior tibial nerve and its branches; surrounding tissue inflammation does not establish a separate damaged organ.
Dystroglycan glycosylation disorder with progressive skeletal muscle degeneration and defining intellectual disability; severe intellectual disability is frequent (30-79%).
